key_insight: Seemingly different short mode-evolution coupler designs share one two-mode design space, with equivalent counter-diabatic realizations offering the same bandwidth.
engineering_relevance: A lithography-aware rule broadens high-efficiency optical transfer by narrowing waveguide spacing at the anticrossing and using exact counter-diabatic control to suppress residual nonadiabatic coupling.
method: Unify width, spacing, and axis-bending designs using exact two-mode coupled-mode theory in the Kramers–Henneberger frame.
Relate bandwidth to the integrated light–steering-field misalignment on the Bloch sphere.
Evaluate designs with polymer-platform BPM simulations, particle swarm optimization, and three-dimensional BCB waveguide BPM.
evidence_signal: BPM simulations predict >99% transfer across 274 nm for a 500 µm coupler with a 1.05 µm minimum edge gap, versus 150 nm for a fixed-spacing-reference CD design at nearly the same gap; numerical optimization did not outperform the design rule.
watch_item: Evidence is simulation-based; fabricated-device bandwidth and sensitivity to manufacturing tolerances remain to be validated.
paper_title: Unified design of short mode-evolution couplers
